def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    frame = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row),
                key=lambda v: sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))

    # Find full-width and full-height frame lines.
    rs = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == frame for v in grid[r]) >= w - 2]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == frame for r in range(h)) >= h - 2]

    # Colors placed at the intersections encode the cells of the reduced grid.
    markers = {}
    for r in rs:
        for c in cs:
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != frame:
                markers[r, c] = v

    other = [v for row in grid for v in row if v != frame]
    fill = min(set(other), key=other.count) if other else 0

    out = []
    for r1, r2 in zip(rs, rs[1:]):
        row = []
        for c1, c2 in zip(cs, cs[1:]):
            corners = [markers.get((r, c)) for r, c in
                       ((r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2))]
            row.append(corners[0] if corners[0] is not None and
                       all(v == corners[0] for v in corners) else fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter

    # The repeated background and the regularly spaced separator color
    # define a lattice. The non-background pixels on separator lines are
    # the encoded output cells.
    counts = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row)
    bg = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    sep_rows = [r for r in range(h)
                if sum(x == bg for x in grid[r]) >= w - 2]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w)
                if sum(grid[r][c] == bg for r in range(h)) >= h - 2]

    # Keep internal separator rows and read the marker pattern at each
    # successive separator-column position.
    rr = sep_rows[1:-1]
    cc = sep_cols
    if not rr:
        rr = sep_rows
    out = []
    for r in rr:
        vals = []
        for c in cc:
            v = grid[r][c]
            vals.append(v if v != bg else 0)
        # A separator marker is repeated at both ends of a segment;
        # retain one value per segment.
        if len(vals) > 1:
            vals = vals[:-1]
        out.append(vals)

    # Remove empty/background-only margins.
    while out and all(v == 0 for v in out[0]):
        out.pop(0)
    if out:
        keep = [j for j in range(len(out[0])) if any(row[j] != 0 for row in out)]
        out = [[row[j] for j in keep] for row in out]
    return out or [[0]]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    cnt = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row)
    frame = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Each separator intersection carries a marker; the marker pattern
    # is the compact output grid.
    rs = [r for r in range(h) if sum(x == frame for x in grid[r]) >= w - 2]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == frame for r in range(h)) >= h - 2]
    bg = cnt.most_common(2)[1][0]

    result = []
    for r in rs:
        row = []
        for c in cs:
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v == frame:
                v = bg
            row.append(v)
        result.append(row)

    # Return the marker-containing portion, excluding outer boundary.
    return [row[:-1] for row in result[1:]]
